gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that the two Keychron full-size picks differ about 3× in implied battery draw on Keychron's own figures (K5 Max 2,000 mAh / 95 h, K5 Ultra 8K 2,600 mAh / 370 h), or that 'full size' covers 108 keys on a Keychron K5 Max but 100 keys on a Lofree Flow Lite 2 100.
standout_why: Novelty is only checked against purchase.fyi, the one rival page whose body I could read. It gives the K5 Max a single honorable-mention line ('100% layout') with no key count, battery or size figure, and names no other board with a number pad. The RTINGS best-list and K5 Max review returned only navigation, and Technobezz (the page cited for the K5 Ultra 8K) returned HTTP 403, so they may already carry these figures. The backlight and connection conditions behind each battery-hours claim, which would be the real footnote, could not be read: keychron.com, lofree.co and nuphy.com product pages returned HTTP 429.
decides: It confirms a Keychron as the pick and leans to the K5 Ultra 8K over the K5 Max: about 3.9× the claimed hours for $15.75 more ($86.99 vs $71.24), with a footprint about 11% larger at the same 720 g. That lean holds only if both hour figures use the same backlight condition, which I could not read. The Lofree Flow Lite 2 100 meets the page's line (98-108 keys) on Lofree's own 'full-size 100-key' wording, but it has 8 fewer keys than the K5 Max, a 100-hour claim, and costs $95.20 at checkout against $71.24-$86.99 for the Keychrons. On these figures it does not take the top spot; it places only as the 100-key alternative.
